The [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Calculate a proportional height and simplified aspect ratio from pixel dimensions. Enter your width, height and new width and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Calculate a proportional height and simplified aspect ratio from pixel dimensions. This free online aspect ratio calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Aspect Ratio Calculator

Start by entering your width (px), then entering your height (px) and finally entering your new width (px). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your width (px).
2. Enter your height (px).
3. Enter your new width (px).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

New height = new width × original height ÷ original width.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 1920 × 1080 is 16:9; at 1280 pixels wide the height is 720. Try the same figures in the [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Width: 1920 px, Height: 1080 px, New width: 1280 px), the [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) returns New height: 720 px, Simplified ratio: 16 : 9, Decimal ratio: 1.777778. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this aspect ratio calculator free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the Aspect Ratio Calculator use?

New height = new width × original height ÷ original width. You can see it in action in the [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Aspect Ratio Calculator?

Just Width, Height and New width. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
